title: Optimize console econ strategy with Harlequin Finance
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Harlequin through the Optimize console cost simulator focusing on batching and prefix/KV cache configurations. Discussed Harlequin's real-time alerts workload, target SLOs, expected monthly tokens (~2M), and peak concurrency. SE proposed a hybrid approach: modest batching + high prefix cache hit rates for interactive latency budgets, plus a pilot on dedicated capacity for peak windows. Next steps include Redwood running a tailored console sim with Harlequin token traces and sharing security docs.

Harlequin to provide a 7-day sample of production traces (anonymized) by 2027-08-04

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Recording: Fireflies.ai auto

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we have Maya and Ravi from Redwood, Liam is here too. happy to run through the Optimize console workflow and then dig into your specific numbers. Tara, Marcus, can you confirm audio?
[00:12] Tara Lin: yep good here, thanks Maya. we got Evan and Sofia on as well. excited to see how batching and cache could bring down costs for our alerts.
[01:05] Ravi Kapoor: cool quick agenda, 1) brief workload review 2) console cost sim walkthrough 3) batching + prefix/KV recommendations 4) pilot proposal and next steps. sound ok?
[01:25] Marcus D'Angelo: yep that's perfect. for context we run a real-time trade alerts service, average prompt length is about 80 tokens, responses average 120 tokens, roughly 2 million tokens per month today, spikes up to 40 rps during market opens.
[02:10] Liam O'Neill: thanks Marcus. couple clarifying Qs — is there session affinity today? are you keeping user conversation state server-side or in the client?
[02:28] Marcus D'Angelo: we keep last 3 turns client-side, but we do want server-side KV cache for quick prefetches of static user profile info and market snapshots.
[03:15] Ravi Kapoor: okay good. so the two levers that matter for your workload are batching (which improves throughput/cost per token) and prefix/KV caching (which can reduce decode tokens by supplying precomputed context). for interactive services you usually balance small batch windows with high cache hit rates to keep p95 latency under 250ms.
[05:40] Tara Lin: what's a realistic batch size given our 40 rps spikes? we can't tolerate long tail latency.
[06:05] Ravi Kapoor: right — for 40 rps peak and short prompts, we recommend micro-batching (10-30ms wait) which gives effective batch sizes in the single digits at peak but allows higher batching during quieter periods. the console sim we ran during the call — this is approximate — showed throughput gains of ~1.6x with micro-batching and no perceptible latency regression for p95 in a 200-300ms SLO.
[08:15] Marcus D'Angelo: can you show the console sim numbers live?
[08:25] Maya Chen: yeah I'll share screen. the cost simulator has inputs: tokens/month, prompt/response lengths, peak rps, desired p95 SLO, and cache hit profile. we plugged in Harlequin's numbers earlier.
[09:05] [screen share noise]
[09:20] Ravi Kapoor: so baseline hosted with no cache and single-request mode is ~ $0.021 per 1k tokens (example numbers), with your 2M tokens that's about $42/mo in this simplified view. adding micro-batching brings it down to ~$27/mo in sim (due to better GPU utilization) and a prefix cache with 65% hit rate drops it further to ~$12/mo. these are ballpark to illustrate relative savings.
[11:45] Sofia Romero: that delta is big. how realistic is 65% cache hit for our app?
[12:10] Ravi Kapoor: depends on how much of the prompt can be prefetched — static profile info, market snapshot snippets, and templated instructions are high hit candidates. some customers see 50-80% for similar use cases after a warmup period. we should test with your traces.
[15:30] Tara Lin: what about KV vs prefix cache? we get confused between the two in our team.
[15:50] Liam O'Neill: quick shorthand — prefix cache stores entire token prefixes frequently used in the model input, KV cache stores model key/value states for autoregressive decoding speedups in session contexts. for your short-turn alerts a prefix cache often yields the largest token savings because you reuse the same instruction + market snapshot tokens. KV helps when sessions have long hidden state across turns.
[18:20] Marcus D'Angelo: any changes required on our side to support prefix caching?
[18:40] Ravi Kapoor: minor — you need to tag repeatable prefix segments on the client or via a proxy, and Redwood's runtime can handle lookup + merge. we can add heuristics to auto-detect frequent prefixes in the pilot.
[21:00] Evan Brooks: on security — we need SOC2 + KMS integration. are there any blockers for a private deployment?
[21:30] Maya Chen: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and on-prem options. SOC2 is in our pack, we'll share the security docs. typical path: start with hosted pilot, validate econ, then move to Dedicated or Private for data residency/KMS if needed.
[24:10] Tara Lin: ok procurement will want cost delta for Dedicated vs Hosted as well as SLA impacts.
[24:40] Maya Chen: got it, we'll include a side-by-side: unit cost, reserved capacity pricing, typical throughput SLOs, and SLA language in the follow-up.
[27:00] Ravi Kapoor: back to the sim — here's a slightly more detailed run: when we simulate a prefix hit rate ramp from 0% to 80% the marginal token cost drops nonlinearly; with 80% hit you approach 80-85% lower token decode cost, but you trade off added complexity in pipeline and slightly higher memory usage for cache indexes.
[29:55] Marcus D'Angelo: memory usage — what's the footprint for a 10k active user set?
[30:10] Ravi Kapoor: rough order: 10k prefixes hashed, depends on average prefix length, but think tens to low hundreds of MB for indexes and a few GB if you store warm KV blocks. we can profile with your traces.
[33:00] Tara Lin: any risks to model quality from aggressive caching or quantization choices?
[33:25] Liam O'Neill: caching prefixes doesn't change the model, it just feeds repeated tokens; quantization can affect quality — Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles per model and flags quality regressions via evals. we'll bring those eval reports to the pilot.
[36:10] Sofia Romero: on the pilot — what's acceptance criteria? we want cost reduction without >5% regression in alert correctness or >10% increase in false positives.
[36:35] Maya Chen: that sounds reasonable. recommended pilot metrics: token cost reduction %, p95 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, model quality measured against your annotation set, and cache hit rate. we can bake those into the pilot runbook.
[40:05] Marcus D'Angelo: what about model routing fallback — if cache misses or model overload occurs, do you have automatic fallback?
[40:30] Ravi Kapoor: yes smart routing can fallback to a cheaper variant or another region; policies are configurable per route so during peak we can keep a high-priority route for critical alerts.
[44:00] Tara Lin: could you show an example config in the console for batching + cache thresholds?
[44:18] Maya Chen: sure, screen— this is a ruleset: target p95, max batch delay 30ms, min batch size 1, cache TTL 60s for market snapshot, prefix eviction heuristics LRU with frequency boost. you can tune this per model/route.
[47:20] Evan Brooks: procurement question — if we go Dedicated, what commit levels are typical?
[47:45] Maya Chen: typical reserved capacity starts at a monthly commit to match 70-80% of expected sustained traffic. we can do burst buffers for spikes. we'll outline tradeoffs in the pricing doc.
[51:10] Ravi Kapoor: last technical note — warmup strategies matter. prefetching market snapshots just before market open yields high hit rates during the critical window. also session affinity helps KV reuse across a user's quick back-and-forth.
[55:00] Tara Lin: we can supply a 7-day trace and a sample of our deployment schedule, looks like the next market stress day is 2027-08-10 so we'd like pilot before that.
[56:15] Maya Chen: perfect, we'll aim to have the console sim back to you by 2027-08-06 and propose a pilot kickoff week of 2027-08-09.
[58:30] Sofia Romero: quick Q about logging — do we get token-level usage and audit logs for compliance?
[58:50] Liam O'Neill: yes console has token-level breakdowns, per-route traces and audit logs. for Private we can push logs to your SIEM.
[60:05] Marcus D'Angelo: that's great. one last thing — can you include a sample risk mitigations note about stale cache causing old snapshots?
[60:20] Ravi Kapoor: yes — TTLs, explicit invalidation hooks on data changes, and versioned prefixes are common mitigations. we'll include that in the runbook.
[61:00] Maya Chen: awesome thanks everyone, recap: Harlequin to send traces by 8/4, Redwood to run sim by 8/6, pricing and security pack by 8/5, pilot kickoff week of 8/9. thanks all, we'll follow up in email.
[61:30] Meeting end.
